says: The dredging gangs of the lower channel are hired out of Alten Corimont.

The An-Xileel drove the Empire out of Black Marsh.
The An-Xileel are the nativist government of Argonia.

Other Argonians hate the Archeins for selling their own people.

The neck is the only dry line between the meres for a long way.
For about fifty metres the mere covers the north half of the road, knee-deep and in places to the waist.
If the meres dried back, the poles would be left standing on dry ground.
Nobody would replace the poles.

says: Archon has marsh to the north and beaches to the south.
The harbour authority's power stops at the headland.
Archon is the eastern port and the province's legal harbour.
Pilot families bring ships into Archon through the estuary approach.
Argonia is a marsh country.
Black Marsh took the name Argonia when it left the Empire.
Argonia is ruled from inside the marsh, not by an emperor.
Argonians have a natural gift for magic and for stealth.
The Argonians are the lizard-folk native to Black Marsh.
Saxhleel is the Argonians' own word for themselves.
The sap of its Hist makes each tribe look a little different.
One smokes hides at the fire while the rest sleep.
One of the band stands at the gate totems.
The band works in turns.
One watches the bend and whistles when a walker comes into view.

The Emperor would not send soldiers into the interior after the survivors.

Families live in the Rose now.

The Blackwood Road climbs through Blackwood to Cyrodiil.
A boat crew poles and loads its boat along the channel.
A boat crew sleeps at whatever landing the boat reaches by dark.

A timber house stands on posts.

The mud is sucking.
A bloom struck gives a hollow ring.
Sulphur hangs in the air.
The furnace stands on a levelled floor above the seep.

A small timber house stands west of the furnace.
The seep lies below the bank.
Bog iron forms in the ground here.

The diggers come from three villages for one season a year.
The diggers consider the work shameful.

The seep is stagnant and rich in iron.
The ore is lifted from the mud in cakes.
The workings would be abandoned without ceremony.

says: The seep is being worked out, and each season's cakes lie further from the path.

Bog iron forms in stagnant water rich in iron.
Families driven from the foraging live at the hiring camp a kilometre east.

The road keeps to the dry strip at the mountain foot.
The road crosses two reaches of the river marsh, where the water stands up to a metre and a quarter deep.
A stone causeway would replace the planks if anyone paid for one.

says: The Bretons are a human people of the west.
Bretic means of the Bretons.
An Argonian calls a Breton traveller an ojel.
The Bright-Throats seal an alliance with a bonding ceremony.
The Bright-Throats breed horse-lizards.
The Bright-Throats welcome outsiders.

The column's men take a levy from the road below the camp.

claim: A locked chest beside the old stable holds salvage held back from the count.

claim: The square yard wall reads through scrub from the road bend.

The way-station has a straight ridge and a square yard wall.
Chasepoint is an Imperial road stage east of Soulrest.

The wreck-salvage families keep the stage.

The roof is Argonian reed thatch on Imperial walls.
Chasepoint stands on the last firm ground before the coast road turns inland.
Wreckage from the Southern Sea comes ashore on the coast to the south.

says: The wreck on the bar carried bonded labourers below deck, so the families will not work it.

claim: The village is the road's water point at the ford.

The landing half will not help to repair the well in stone.

The village blames the salt works for the salt in the water.

Helstrom lies south-west of the spring, past the village of Ux-Aneet.

Argonians drink the sap of the Hist.
The sap shapes the child's body and scales for life.

A silent Hist has stopped speaking to its tribe.

The remnant pursue the house's northern interests.
House Dres built its wealth on Argonian slaves.
The Empire built roads, road stages and prisons.
The Empire held the coasts and borders of Black Marsh but not the deep marsh.
The Empire withdrew from Black Marsh.

claim: A unique item lies in the lair.
A hidden cache lies in the lair.

claim: The landing's clay basket lies at the cut, where the crocodile came up.

The one charge would be 2 drakes a stop, 1 to each bank, the landing's drake paying for its clay behind the lining, renewed each dry season.

A cutting is a piece taken from a Hist and planted away from the tree.
The Unbound Root takes cuttings from a Hist.
The Unbound Root puts the Hist above every law.
Some of the Unbound Root are victims of state abuse and some are fanatics.
The Unbound Root says real change needs a way to sever the bond.

claim: The village gives provisions to a stranger who brings news.
The tree stands nine bends upriver. Its minder says it has begun to go quiet.
The tree is a day upriver from the camp where the families' clutch is kept.
Something at Nine Bends records its past.
Nine Bends tells part of the province's past.
A quest starts or turns at Nine Bends.
Someone at Nine Bends has work for the player.
Nine Bends gives shelter for the night.
Talk at Nine Bends points to something elsewhere.
A traveller can rest safely at Nine Bends.
A player can buy and sell at Nine Bends.
The tree's chimes carry a bend downstream of the village.
The village is kept up by too few hands.
One wooden landing stage stands on the river.
The mood is quiet; there are too few people for the size of it.
The reed and fern are wet green and the trunk bark is dark and wet.
Painted clay urns stand at the hatchery.
The air smells of sap and wet reed.
The tree still talks, a low sound.
A hatchery pool is cut into the bank so the tree's roots run down into it.
One broad low tree stands with the village built round its foot in a ring.
The river bends away on both sides of the village.
A tribe keeps a tree here. The gang families answer to it.
The village hires its people out downriver to the gangs of Alten Corimont.
The work has been a day downriver for sixty years.
The tribe keeps a tree and hires its own people out downriver, because there is no other coin here.
More of the village's adults are on a downriver roll each year.
The village stands on firm bank above the salt wedge, where the water is fresh enough to drink.
Nine bends of river lie between the village and the port.
If the tree withdraws, there is no reason left to keep the village nine bends from the work.
If the tree withdraws, the lower channel is left without a Hist that will speak to it.

says: The Veiled Reed is the covert office of the An-Xileel.
The Veiled Reed's factors travel the interior as its agents.
The Veiled Reed's agents guard the province against its enemies by secrecy and coercion.

claim: A hidden cache holds a unique item: whatever was worth sealing in with it.
Workshop stock, as materials, lies in the main part of the vault.
The vault is entered by a stair-throat.
The party that sealed the door nailed a board to it.
The board says what is inside the vault, and it is still legible.
A quest could establish what has been fed to the sealed vault, on whose orders.
Something at The Sealed Vault has to be fought.
The Sealed Vault has a way down into a delve.
Goods are stored at The Sealed Vault for a player to find.
Something at The Sealed Vault records its past.
A unique item is kept at The Sealed Vault.
The vault is sealed and posted.
The stone is grey and the board weathered.
Iron straps are welded across the stone door.
The message on the nailed board is legible after two hundred years.
A vault lies under a ruined works.
The vault was sealed by the people who found what had grown in it.
The sealing party left the door welded.
The voriplasm has been sealed in the vault for two hundred years.
The sealing party's note is still nailed to the door and names what is inside.
The vault is a stone undercroft with one door and no other opening.
If the vault were opened, a creature would be released.
The province has a specific and unhappy history with that creature.

says: A traveller asks the well-keeper before drawing water.
The station well is Imperial-built stone.
The well is drawn by a windlass at set hours.
White Rose Prison holds the graves of Argonians who died mid-Owing, far from their Hist.
A witness knows every family and every name on the roll.
The witness can say who saw a thing done in the camp.
The roll is read out on the barge and never in the camp.
More adults go downriver on the roll each year.
The roll is the list of debtors in the dredging gang.
Most xanmeers are ruins.
A xanmeer is a stepped stone pyramid built by the old Argonians.
The insides of a xanmeer are mazes of traps and relics.
The Xit-Xaht's Hist directs the tribe.
The other tribes fear the Xit-Xaht.
The Xit-Xaht still build in stone.
